project.title: Local AI Servers Can Reduce Manufacturing AI Costs and Infrastructure Requirements

scope: qualitative public private hybrid cloud distinctions
resource scheduling and monitoring field candidates
AI adoption by industry and region
above-designated-size manufacturing AI adoption above 30 percent
current China intelligent-compute demand distribution by broad user industry
China total AI IT spending CAGR
C29 process control and defect inspection
Korean steel cement paper and metal factories

contract.gap: Existing work does not jointly compare factory-distributed, group-pooled, regional multi-node, industry-centralized, and hierarchical AI architectures under equal service while tracing multi-voltage-level grid expansion and bounded factory rooftop PV.
contract.task: Develop and later evaluate a task-driven compute-energy-grid planning model for factory- and industry-level distributed LLM deployment.
outcomes: cost incidence by enterprise type, industry, region, and actor

questions.text: Under equal AI service, when do distributed, pooled, or hierarchical architectures reduce grid expansion and total system cost relative to one industry data center?

Under equal AI service, can asymmetric regulatory treatment of local AI assets and cloud operating expenses make a regulated enterprise favor local deployment when cloud has lower market direct cost or customer revenue requirement?

Across Chinese manufacturing industries and regions, how do enterprise organization, AI adoption, task mobility, local energy resources, and shared-compute scale change the enterprise and social costs of local, group-pooled, regional, and cloud deployment?

contract.contribution: Integrate workload placement, utilization-calibrated server power, a zero-existing-headroom-credit grid-capacity boundary, layered grid expansion, bounded rooftop PV, on-site water, cooling, noise, land and site postprocessing, and multi-node siting in one conditional planning framework.
nonclaims: Distributed deployment is not presumed superior.
Rooftop PV nameplate capacity is not treated as firm grid capacity.
Scenario screening is not presented as an empirical industry-wide result.
The US paper's spatial findings are not transferred directly to China.
A 2024 server-platform roadmap does not determine current or future technology parameters and does not replace enterprise-site-grid architecture design.

semantic_locks.text: All architecture comparisons provide the same effective AI service subject to common quality, latency, reliability, and data-boundary constraints.
Factory PV capacity is bounded by projected roof area times technical density times a separate realization ratio.

style_profile.language_variant: English main formula note; Chinese internal design files

facts.value: The source study models operational Scope 1 water and Scope 2 grid water and carbon, while excluding embodied Scope 3 impacts from its primary spatial analysis.

alignment.method: Joint task assignment, utilization-based server power, facility PUE/WUE, DER dispatch, multi-layer grid expansion, and architecture cost optimization.
alignment.evidence: The active single-case screen uses the EWELD C28 U219 measured weekday shape, a token-derived 2030 integrated text/agent workload, three deployment modes, and deterministic battery and accounting checks. The earlier 24-scenario synthetic high-workload prototype is retained as historical stress-test evidence.
alignment.result: In the active typical machinery case, enterprises prefer local deployment while reconstructed social resource cost modestly favors cloud; the roughly 3 kW local AI increment does not approach the assumed 1.25 MW enterprise connection limit even without DER.
alignment.interpretation: The private-social wedge persists after replacing the reverse-engineered 25-server workload, but it is much smaller; the earlier strong enterprise grid-expansion benefit was driven by a deliberately tight connection and an overstated AI workload rather than a representative manufacturing mechanism.
alignment.limitation: The load shape is measured but scaled to 1 MW; employee count, roof, DER, and connection capacity are scenario assumptions; L20 throughput, visual AI, cloud physical cost, PUE/WUE, and project-level grid cost remain to be calibrated.
alignment.contribution: Separates compute efficiency, energy use, water and carbon footprints, aggregate grid expansion, and maximum single-point expansion.

alignment.method: Twelve-year deterministic revenue-requirement and shareholder-incentive screen comparing the commercial group local AI center with public cloud under changes in cloud price, rate-base eligibility, allowed-return spread, recovery lag, prudence disallowance, and technical obsolescence.
alignment.evidence: At 75% of the current cloud price, cloud market direct cost is RMB 1.506 million per year below local. With full local rate-base eligibility, no lag or stranded balance, and allowed ROE one percentage point above equity cost, local adds RMB 0.665 million of shareholder economic present value while raising equivalent annual customer revenue requirement by RMB 0.804 million relative to cloud.
alignment.result: Asymmetric treatment can reverse the shareholder ranking in a clean scenario, while one-year recovery lag or partial loss of undepreciated assets removes the economic advantage at a one-percentage-point return spread even though local assets still generate accounting earnings.
alignment.interpretation: Regulatory capital preference is plausible as an accounting-profit mechanism, but its conversion into shareholder economic value depends on approval, timing, and obsolescence rules; it is not established as observed enterprise behavior.
alignment.limitation: Cloud procurement price is not cloud social resource cost; Chinese AI server rate-base eligibility, depreciation, recovery lag, and management objectives are uncalibrated placeholders.
alignment.contribution: Separates market direct cost, customer revenue requirement, accounting earnings, and shareholder economic value, identifying the conditions under which their deployment rankings diverge.

alignment.method: Version v0.6.1 is the active national manufacturing screening run. It uses 31 industry-specific bottom-up effective-service demands, six task classes, a continuous 168-hour representative week, representative group shares and factory counts, industry base-load profiles, and a common PyPSA/Linopy/HiGHS capacity-dispatch formulation for independent-factory, representative-group, and single-host industry-pool architectures. Each node's existing grid capacity is fixed to its no-AI baseline peak, prohibiting credit for unobserved contract, transformer, or feeder headroom. The completed workflow contains 31 no-AI baselines and 31 times three IF, IG, and II_1host architecture cases. All 124 optimizations use a Guangdong representative-week day-ahead retail price vector and existing rooftop PV at the representative roof limit; storage remains endogenous. Installed and online server groups are continuous equivalent capacities. No-flexibility ablation and the former separate spot/PV test remain optional diagnostics. The model retains the simplified 32B AWQ lifecycle layer and selects the evidence-bounded conservative compute case (0.416897 accelerator-hour per service unit) jointly with a 1.50 kW dual-L20 maximum server wall-power boundary. No global or output multiplier is used. External 8/14/28 TWh allocations validate national scale but do not define architecture electricity.
alignment.evidence: All C13-C43 divisions have model-ready service, load-shape, group-scale, flexibility, compute-efficiency, lifecycle, and external-allocation inputs. The workflow produced 93 scenario optimizations and verified within every industry that all three architectures reconstruct the same service, preserve full-week storage state, meet 72-hour deadlines, satisfy server/replica/storage constraints, and reconcile lifecycle costs; the national aggregate is 95,544,802.789 effective-service units per day in every architecture. All three national optimized totals lie inside the external 8-28 TWh envelope. The workflow also validates 31-industry same-service GPU-IaaS payment comparisons, 93 industry-architecture hourly base-load alignment profiles, a nationwide IF no-flexibility counterfactual, and a C40 representative-group test using 168 hourly Guangdong day-ahead prices plus 0.25426875 CNY/kWh retail volumetric adders and a separate maximum-demand charge. The per-industry plus/minus 25% allocation comparison is diagnostic only; 17 of 31 industries lie inside that warning band.
alignment.result: The completed and validated v0.6.1 national run reconstructs 95,544,802.789 effective-service units per day in each architecture. IF, IG, and II_1host each use 14.194244 TWh/year of AI-facility electricity and 912,825.087 equivalent installed server groups at the active continuous-capacity boundary. Their zero-existing-headroom-credit incremental grid-expansion screens are respectively 0.0 MW, 10.667 MW, and 1,202.408 MW, and annual incremental modeled costs are RMB 69.439 billion, RMB 68.317 billion, and RMB 68.422 billion. The large single host remains a concentration upper bound rather than an observed cloud location. v0.6.0 numerical series are historical old-boundary results and are not used for active capacity claims. At the current dual-L20 public-price proxy, cloud payment comparisons remain conditional and separate from cloud social resource cost.
alignment.interpretation: Representative-group pooling is the core scenario because it captures server and fixed-cost sharing within a plausible organizational boundary while retaining independent-factory and single-industry-host scenarios as dispersed and concentrated bounds. Under the current high-utilization workload, public-retail GPU-IaaS payments exceed IG owned cost, but this is an enterprise-payment result rather than a cloud social-cost comparison. AI task execution is mildly anticorrelated with industry base load, yet shared facilities are almost flat baseloads. The flat-tariff flexibility ablation and the C40 hourly spot-price test jointly support a conditional mechanism interpretation: preserving high server-asset utilization and avoiding server stock currently dominate electricity-price arbitrage; the modeled energy and demand price signals induce limited peak avoidance but not material active compute-electricity coordination. Server capital cost is a leading explanation rather than a separately identified causal effect until capex, online-reserve, shutdown-capability, and price-spread sensitivities are run.
alignment.limitation: The 31-division outputs remain representative-week screening scenarios, not forecasts or physical network estimates. The v0.6.0 compute and server-power settings form a joint high-electricity boundary, not a measured hardware mean or a 2030 point forecast, and its grid-capacity numbers predate the v0.6.1 zero-headroom-credit decision. The cloud screen uses linearly derived dual-L20 public-price proxies and excludes negotiated discounts, API/SaaS charges, network, storage, migration, integration, and option value. Daily profiles repeat within the week; industry buckets assume internal sharing of load, roof, and storage; and the industry-pool single host is a concentration upper bound. The new capacity boundary is deliberately conservative and does not represent observed contractual or physical spare capacity. The C40 spot-price result is one Guangdong group-scale representative week, combines wholesale prices with April 2026 regulated adders, and omits contract portfolios, deviation settlement, retail-service spreads, and risk; it cannot establish a universal Chinese tariff response. Industry-equivalent noncoincident credits are not national coincident peak reductions or avoided physical grid projects, and mechanism attribution still needs server-capex, online-reserve, shutdown, price-spread, no-PV, and no-storage sensitivities. Only 17 of 31 industries lie inside the external allocation warning band. AI timing is researcher-constructed, some load curves and task templates are borrowed, and the current two-hour storage cost remains an open robustness issue. Province, site, feeder, detailed KV/cache/cold-start behavior, multi-model state, RAG project costs, and social externalities remain outside the current model.
alignment.contribution: Provides the first reproducible nationwide equal-service comparison across factory, representative-group, and industry-pool deployment scales while preserving explicit screening boundaries.
